subject: Web Development
title: HTTP: How Browsers Talk to Servers
description: Learn HTTP: How Browsers Talk to Servers in one minute.

hook.text: When you click a link, your browser sends a message to a server asking for a page.

buildup.text: That message follows HTTP, a protocol Tim Berners-Lee wrote in 1991.

discovery.text: HTTP is like a polite chat: the browser requests, and the server responds.

twist.text: Early HTTP opened a new connection for every file. Images meant dozens of handshakes.

climax.text: HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 fixed this, letting pages load in a fraction of a second.

punchline.text: The web runs on a 1991 conversation style.

quiz.question: What problem did early HTTP have?
options: A new connection for every file
